findings.issue: Used `pkill -f <pattern>` twice where the pattern matched its own `bash -c` command line, killing its own shell (exit 143); the mistake was diagnosed at turn 32 but repeated at turn 48
findings.suggestion: Kill by PID captured from `ps`/`$!`, or use `pkill -f -o`/exclude $$; never repeat a pattern already known to self-match

findings.issue: Explicitly unsure about Nuxt 4's srcDir/serverDir and Nitro route-file naming but never checked the docs or skills, and the guessed route name (`server/api/index.get.ts` → expected `/api/index`) caused the only test-failing bug
findings.suggestion: When a framework detail is uncertain, spend one turn on the official docs (Nitro server-route naming) before writing code

findings.issue: Sloppy background-server one-liner with leftover placeholder text and mismatched ports (started API on 9200 while probing 9100/3100), creating avoidable confusion
findings.suggestion: Write server start commands deliberately: one port constant, capture PIDs to files, and echo the bound URL before probing

findings.issue: Compared screenshots from a stale build because the new app silently failed to bind port 3200 (old PID still running); briefly suspected its own fix of being broken
findings.suggestion: Check `/tmp/app.log` or the 'Listening on' line after every start, and record PIDs so restarts are verifiable

findings.issue: Wrote TypeScript throughout but never ran a typecheck (measured typechecks: 0); the test suite and build were the only static gates
findings.suggestion: Add `nuxi typecheck` to the loop after the first build and before finishing

summary: A disciplined, linear session: thorough upfront research (spec, tests, screenshots, numeric validation of data assumptions), one architecture that held up, and a single systematic fix cycle for the only real bug. Verification went beyond the tests with visual comparison against reference screenshots and live-overlay runs, including a final full pass after cleanup. The deductions are self-inflicted shell sloppiness — killing its own shell with pkill twice — and skipping framework docs on details it knew it was unsure about.
